clue.text: Only one T in title — that's old-fashioned

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the honour that follows

parts.note: OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour, a title after a name
a sole thing is the only one of its kind

explanation.surface: A pedant notes that a word spelt with just one T has fallen out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the only-one word with T inside the title; OBE is a British honour (Officer of the Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in use is outdated, so describing it as passé fits.

clue.text: One bereft of real parents has almost no origins

definitions.text: One bereft of real parents has almost no origins

indicators.note: origins asks for the first letters of the clue words, their beginnings

explanation.surface: A child without parents has almost no family background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' takes the first letters of One, real, parents, has, almost, no; 'bereft of' is skipped as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A child whose mother and father are dead has lost both parents.

clue.text: Having run into a man, learner drivers show deference

indicators.note: Having run into says the following pieces go inside the man's name

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
L is the learner sign on British cars
AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring body for drivers

explanation.surface: After crashing into a pedestrian, novice motorists bow politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having run into' sends A, the learner and the drivers inside the man; the answer is used as a verb, to bow low in greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow of respect in Muslim cultures, used as a verb for bowing respectfully.

clue.text: Hurry up and catch shark damaged in 23

indicators.note: in says the rearranged fish goes within the 23 answer's synonym

parts.note: the answer to 23 across is a loop of rope

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of shark are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An urgent call to move fast and capture an injured fish in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the fish, and 'in' puts that inside a loop, the 23 answer; 'catch' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to be quick and alert is telling them to get a move on.

clue.text: What you will number when it's dark

parts.note: twelfth is an ordinal number
night is the time when it is dark

explanation.surface: Choose any number you like after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What You Will' is the subtitle of Shakespeare's comedy, so the definition is a title, not a phrase about choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy carries the alternative title 'What You Will'.

clue.text: Chap about to acquire wound

indicators.note: about means the man's name goes around the next piece

parts.note: Ted is a typical man's name, standing for any chap
to win something is to acquire it

explanation.surface: A man is on the point of picking up an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind, as yarn is coiled round; 'about' wraps the chap round the win.
explanation.definitionFit: Thread that has been coiled or twisted round is said to be wound.

clue.text: Consider carefully, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: of speaking says the word for a manner is heard, not written

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Think it over, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in a manner of speaking' hides the parse: 'a manner' is WAY, and 'of speaking' gives its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or assess the merits of something is to balance them.

clue.text: Bid to avoid verbal rough play

parts.note: not expresses avoidance or negation

indicators.note: verbal says the word for rough play is heard, not seen

parts.note: romps are boisterous rough play

explanation.surface: An attempt to escape a spoken scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT, then RUMPS, which sounds like ROMPS in a clipped accent.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a contract with no suit as trumps is a call at auction.

clue.text: Untidy she-devil, very untidy

indicators.note: very untidy says the letters are thoroughly disordered

explanation.surface: A slovenly she-devil is very messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' is a verb here, to mess up; 'very untidy' rearranges SHE-DEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle or disarrange hair or clothes is to mess them up.

clue.text: Go to the roadside for this garment

definitions.meaning: to steer a vehicle to the edge of the road and stop
a knitted top slipped on over the head, a jumper

explanation.surface: A driver stopping at the kerb to put on some clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver halting at the kerb does this manoeuvre, and a knitted jumper worn over the head carries the same name.

clue.text: Opening strike grips a country

indicators.note: grips means the word for strike holds the next piece within it

parts.note: to hit is to strike
US, the United States, is a country

explanation.surface: Industrial action takes hold of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' is a gap, a noun, not a beginning; 'grips' puts A inside the strike, and the country follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or break in continuity is an opening.

clue.text: Marks on side of ship made by pump cable

parts.note: a plimsoll is a canvas shoe also called a pump
a line is a cable or rope

explanation.surface: Markings on a vessel's hull made by a pump and cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pump' looks mechanical; it is a light canvas shoe, which British English also calls a plimsoll.
explanation.definitionFit: The load-line markings painted on a hull show how deep a ship may safely sit.

clue.text: More than one president gave woman a title

definitions.meaning: two US presidents shared this surname, John and John Quincy
in Genesis the first man named his partner, saying she shall be called Woman

explanation.surface: Several heads of state bestowed a title on a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as the first man's deed: in Genesis 2:23 he said she shall be called Woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Two American presidents bore the surname, plural here, and the Biblical first man, in Genesis, named his partner Woman.

clue.text: A good hand from the largest possible audience

definitions.meaning: in poker, three of a kind with a pair is a strong hand
a theatre with every seat sold

explanation.surface: A fine round of cards comes from a packed crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker three of a kind plus a pair is a strong holding, and a theatre sold out to every seat has the same name.

clue.text: To sing small note, little Tom must be surrounded by liquor and food

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: must be surrounded by says the little man goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a malt liquor
Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of an English folk tale
a pie is food

explanation.surface: A tiny boy is told to sing quietly while drink and food surround him.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing small is an old British idiom for backing down meekly; 'must be surrounded by' puts the little man inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing down humbly and admitting error is what both phrases describe.

clue.text: What skulkers do — have a lazy morning and defer action

parts.note: to lie in is to stay in bed late
to wait is to hold off acting

explanation.surface: Ambushers stay in bed and put things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushers hide and keep still until their target comes.

clue.text: Bob turns out to be pigheaded.

indicators.note: out says the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bob proves to be an obstinate fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'out' rearranges BOB TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate, unyielding person is mulish.

clue.text: Game runner leads race supported by the French

indicators.note: leads says the runner comes first, before the race
supported by says, in this down clue, the French word sits underneath

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like a sledge's
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
les is French for the

explanation.surface: A runner leads in a race with French backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a ski. SKI leads TT, with LES below.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins, where a ball knocks down wooden pins, is a bowling pastime.

clue.text: Con-con-confine

parts.note: to con is to swindle, or take someone in
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A stammered word about locking someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter splits into two separate words: the verb con (to cheat) and the noun con (a convict).
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing someone and holding them captive is to lock them up.

clue.text: Able to take in water, or soup, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something that absorbs water, perhaps broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OR SOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of tiny holes that let liquid soak through describes a permeable material.

clue.text: Lower note held by churchman

indicators.note: held by says the note sits inside the churchman

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note is sustained by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is a verb, to degrade; 'held by' puts the sol-fa note inside the churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade or debase oneself is to bring oneself down.

clue.text: Arrangement between two people which later both may change

indicators.note: may change says the letters of the two words can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people's agreement that both may alter later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may change' turns LATER BOTH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement to marry is a formal agreement between a couple.

clue.text: Weight it's said you put on at one time

indicators.note: put on says the letter is placed onto, into, the next word

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: it's said means the word you is heard as a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun you

explanation.surface: People say you gained weight once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' makes U from YOU, put into ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixteenth of a pound is a unit of mass.

clue.text: Gin knocked back in a short time by bridge player

indicators.note: knocked back says the word for shortly is read backwards

parts.note: soon means in a short time
E is East, one of the four bridge players

explanation.surface: A bridge player downs a gin quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink; it is a trap or snare. 'knocked back' turns SOON into NOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching game, as is a loop of cord that tightens.

clue.text: Outside broadcast extended out of square

parts.note: long means extended

explanation.surface: A broadcast from outside overran and went askew.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is not square.

clue.text: I got upset with profane opera

indicators.note: got upset says the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is offended by an irreverent opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got upset' rearranges I and PROFANE. HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic stage work.

clue.text: Some of the keenest edges are one inside another

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the sharpest blades lie one within another.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fitted together like Russian dolls sit each within the next.

clue.text: Junk counter is inside

indicators.note: inside says the word is goes within the counter

parts.note: a jetton is a token or counter used in gaming

explanation.surface: A piece of rubbish is found within a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' is a verb, to throw away; 'inside' puts the word is within an old gaming token.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw away or discard cargo, as from a ship, is to dump it.
